key_insight: Portable query generation for job search works best when reward shaping is carefully engineered, because the main failure mode is reward hacking rather than optimizer choice.
engineering_relevance: For industrial semantic search systems, robust deterministic reward rules can be more important than the specific RLAIF optimizer when training query-generation policies.
method: Built an end-to-end RLAIF pipeline for generating portable job-search queries.
Compared critic-free optimizers, including RLOO, REINFORCE++, and GRPO, under adversarial reward conditions.
Added a deterministic rule-based reward floor to penalize verbatim copying and reduce reward hacking.
evidence_signal: On a cross-family evaluation judge, the reward-floor fix produced a +0.147 quality gain, and the training-time reward model inflated apparent gains by 2.4×.
watch_item: GRPO appears especially sensitive to spurious reward signals, so implementations should guard against judge rubric loopholes and copying-based exploitation.
paper_title: Designing Reward Signals for Portable Query Generation: A Case Study in Industrial Semantic Job Search
